payload.description:
## Trigger

When an agent picks up a record in a repository that installed only the tracker kit, I want the record itself to carry acceptance criteria and requirements as typed fields with a gate that refuses unshaped work, so I can verify and validate against the record rather than against my reading of its prose.

Measured 2026-09-18 over this ledger's 1367 created events: 0 carry a requirements field and 28 carry a ## Requirements heading in prose, against a positive control of 467 carrying an acceptance_criteria field and 782 carrying the ## Acceptance Criteria heading. So the zero is the data's and not the probe's. A grep for acceptance or requirement across .basicly/core/kit/tracker/*.py returns nothing: all the shaping lives in src/basicly/invest.py and src/basicly/plan_record.py, which a standalone consumer never receives.

The enforcement point is a definition-of-ready gate rather than a refusal at create. A record is shaped while it is being written, and an import carries records that were never shaped at all, so refusing the write would break the import that basicly-i98ooyo just shipped and would refuse 900 of this ledger's own 1367 records.

Making the ready set itself filter is deliberately NOT in scope and the reason is measured: 900 of 1367 records carry no acceptance field, so a filtering ready set would collapse this repository's own ready count from 274 and stall the engine loop. That becomes worth doing once the backlog is shaped, as its own record.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The kit computes what a record owes - a trigger in either story voice, acceptance criteria, and requirements - reading a typed field first and a prose heading second, so an existing record keeps working.
- create, child and update take --acceptance and --requirements as first-class flags and report what the record still owes.
- A dor verb exits non-zero and names what is missing, so a hook or a skill can gate work on it.
- A record carrying both fields passes the gate, against a control record carrying neither that fails it.

## Requirements

- No engine import: the kit reads its own committed data and takes everything else as an argument.
- Standard library only and no syntax newer than Python 3.9.
- Additive at every existing call site: no current caller of create, update or ready changes behaviour.
payload.title: give the kit the acceptance criteria and requirements an agent verifies against

payload.text:
Third requirement corrected during the build, with the reason. It read 'Additive at every existing call site: no current caller of create, update or ready changes behaviour.' That is not what shipped and stating it unchanged would have been the false claim the last retro added a rule about.

What actually holds: every existing key keeps its meaning and no caller loses a capability, but the write reports gain two keys, owed and remedy. A consumer asserting exact dict equality on a write's JSON sees a change, and this repository's own test_a_swallowed_write_is_reported_not_raised did. Its original assertion is kept as a subset comparison and the new fact is asserted beside it. ready is untouched.

A side effect the pin caught and I had not intended: the first _owed_of went through queries.folded, which is snapshot.load, so a create published the derived snapshot as well as appending. test_the_consumer_writes_only_inside_its_own_directory failed on a stray ledger/snapshot.jsonl. It now folds the events in memory and publishes nothing, which is also the cheaper read.

Making the ready set filter unshaped records stays out of scope for the reason on the record: 900 of this ledger's 1367 records carry no acceptance field, so a filtering ready set would collapse the ready count from 274 and stall the engine loop. dor is the gate; ready still offers everything.

payload.name: close_reason
payload.value: shipped: the kit computes what a record owes, create child and update take the three flags and report it, dor refuses an unshaped record, and every command the agent skill names was run against a real ledger
